chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from some of our companions, from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon them, that they said:

There is no harm in a man performing salat (prayer) in a garment that has blood on it scattered like sprinkles. If its owner had seen it before that, then there is no harm in it so long as it is not gathered together to the measure of a dirham.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing worn in prayer
key_terms.قَدْرَ الدِّرْهَمِ: the legal measure of a dirham used as a threshold
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.مُتَفَرِّقًا: scattered in separate spots rather than concentrated

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in a garment that has a small amount of blood on it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding blood on clothing during salat (prayer). Small, scattered traces of blood do not invalidate the prayer, provided they are not combined into an amount equal to a dirham.
